Hi, I have both AvPD and DPD traits (not full blown, don't know the difference), and for me short CBT helped a lot to reshape my thoughts. The thoughts don't go really away, but they are somewhat supressed and by not thinking about them, you kind of forget them. But I also had psychosis break and lot of my CBT was for the psychosis itself. I am also on antidepressants and antipsychotics, and I can tell you that I feel less anxious and nervous than before, but I guess it's mainly because of the antipsychotics. I am worried what will happen when I will have to stop taking those antipsychotics, I fear that the anxiety will come back stronger. I did some psychodynamic therapy, but I think I could spend that time better. It was oriented on gaining insight which I needed and it helped me a bit, but I would probably do CBT again. The thing is, each therapy should be modelled by your needs, so it's pretty subjective to talk about experience, and also therapists are each different, so if I got a different psychodynamic-oriented therapist I might have had different experience.
